business_scope.primary_industry_name: Handmade Sharp-Edge Epoxy Resin Liquid Core RPG Dice Casting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Common Law corporate statutes modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law, RMI Revised Code, and U.S. Compact-based constitutional law; no Islamic Sharia application
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (2023 Amended Compact)
Agreement between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America for the Exchange of Information with Respect to Taxes (TIEA, effective 2003)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus, in force 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, as amended by the AML/CFT (Amendment) Act 2021; Business Corporations Act 1990, Title 51 RMI Revised Code, as amended; Trust Companies Act 2012; RMI Registrar of Corporations Rules for Maintenance of Beneficial Ownership Information; National AML/CFT Strategy and Risk Assessment

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each incorporator or subscriber before a notary public of the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatories resident in Hague Convention jurisdictions; otherwise consular legalization by the Marshall Islands Consular Office or other competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as Director and Officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed directors and officers before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside the Marshall Islands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Licensed Agent Acceptance and Registered Office Consent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed in the Marshall Islands; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Funds / Source of Wealth Declaration and UBO Identification Form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner and the compliance officer of the registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization required; apostille or consular legalization for foreign signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every proposed shareholder, UBO, director, officer, and registered agent principal against RMI AML/CFT Act schedules, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and domestic RMI sanctions/PEP lists. PEPs, their family members, and close associates are risk-rated as high and require senior management approval plus enhanced ongoing due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations – Corporate Name Search and Reservation System, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro; online submissions through licensed registered agents under the RMI Corporate Registry system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be in English using the Latin alphabet. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into a romanized English form, and only the transliterated name is recorded. The name must be distinguishable from existing registrations and must include a required corporate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant or authorized registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds of distinctiveness and compliance. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may apply to the High Court of the Marshall Islands for judicial review within 30 days after the administrative appeal is denied. The name may be re-reserved for an additional 30-day window after a fresh application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office. The company must maintain a physical registered office in the Marshall Islands, ordinarily at the office of a licensed registered agent, capable of receiving service of process. A virtual mail-forwarding address may be used for supplementary administrative correspondence but cannot replace the physical registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5% to 10% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a non-resident, low-risk business corporation in the handmade tabletop gaming accessories sector. The probability rises above 30% if AML/CFT risk flags, sanctions matches, inconsistent filings, or registered-agent compliance deficiencies are identified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Title 24, Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended); principally Sections 24-10 (Certificate of Incorporation), 24-16 (Lawful Purposes), 24-30 to 24-32 (Registered Agent and Registered Office), 24-40 to 24-44 (Directors), 24-52 (Payment for Shares), and Part IX (Non-Resident Domestic Corporations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Division, Ministry of Justice, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro Atoll; international submissions are effected through licensed registered agents authorized by the Marshall Islands Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Form BCA-1) filed under Section 24-10 of the Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Business Corporations Act for a non-resident business corporation; the certificate of incorporation may authorize a nominal capital (e.g., US$1,000 divided into 1,000 common shares of US$0.001 par value per share), shares may be issued for such consideration as the board determines, and no escrow or trust account is required by RMI law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Certificate of Incorporation, as filed with the Registrar of Corporations, is approved and ratified. RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription and issuance of 1,000 shares of common stock, par value US$0.001 per share, to the initial subscriber. RESOLVED, that the registered office at Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the registered agent named therein are adopted. RESOLVED, that the Bylaws submitted to this meeting are adopted. RESOLVED, that [NAME] as President, [NAME] as Secretary, and [NAME] as Treasurer are appointed as officers. RESOLVED, that the Corporation elects non-resident domestic status and authorizes the execution of all documents and payment of all statutory fees to perfect its incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Verification and Optional Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Division, Ministry of Justice, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search against the RMI corporate index either at the Registry counter in Majuro or through a licensed registered agent; confirm that the proposed name is distinguishable from all active entities and bears a corporate designator such as Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, or an authorized abbreviation. If filing is deferred, submit Form BCA-6 Name Reservation with the prescribed fee for a non-renewable 30-day reservation; otherwise proceed directly to drafting the Certificate of Incorporation using the verified name.
required_dossiers: Name search and availability request
Name Reservation Application (Form BCA-6) if reservation is sought
Copy of applicant passport or government-issued identification
Payment of prescribed name reservation fee, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of confusing similarity with an existing entity, select a fresh alternative name or obtain the written consent of the prior nameholder; if the application is deficient, the Registry issues a deficiency notice and the applicant has 10 business days to cure the defect without losing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial incorporator, notary public, and licensed RMI registered agent; final acceptance rests with the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Certificate of Incorporation under Section 24-10 of the Business Corporations Act stating: (i) the corporate name; (ii) the name of the registered agent and the registered office address in Majuro; (iii) a lawful purpose clause covering the manufacture and global distribution of tabletop gaming accessories, including handmade epoxy-resin dice; (iv) the authorized capital structure; and (v) the name and address of each initial director. Execute the Certificate before a notary public; if executed outside the Republic, the signature may be attested by the registered agent or a consular officer and apostilled where required by banking or downstream licensing processes.
required_dossiers: Drafted Certificate of Incorporation (Form BCA-1)
Notarized execution page and incorporator consents
Passport copy and proof of residential address of each incorporator
Engagement letter with the RMI licensed registered agent
KYC/AML questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a technical correction notice, such as an impermissible purpose clause or defective share structure, prepare and re-file an amended Certificate within 30 days; failure to cure timely may forfeit the original filing date, in which case priority is reset to the re-filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment with the Registrar, Payment of State Fee, and Issuance of Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Certificate of Incorporation together with the statutory filing fee of US$150 for authorized capital not exceeding 50,000 shares and the registered agent's signed consent. Payment is made by wire transfer to the Registry's designated account or via the licensed agent's trust account. The Registrar scrutinizes the instrument against the Business Corporations Act; upon approval, the Registrar assigns a unique corporate number, endorses the Certificate, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the Corporation's formation and separate legal existence.
required_dossiers: Executed Certificate of Incorporation (Form BCA-1)
Registered Agent Consent (Form BCA-2)
Proof of payment of the US$150 statutory filing fee
Cover letter from the licensed registered agent
Copy of the corporate number assignment request, if separately required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for fee shortfall, incomplete attestation, or missing attachments, the Registry issues a query notice to the agent; the deficiency must be cured within 14 business days to avoid full re-submission, and an expedited 24-hour review service is available upon payment of the expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance Actions: First Board Resolution, Bylaws, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors of the Corporation as named in the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the initial directors or act by unanimous written consent. The board adopts the pro-forma first board resolution ratifying the Certificate of Incorporation, approving the subscription and issuance of common shares to the initial subscriber, adopting the Corporation's Bylaws, ratifying the registered agent and registered office, and appointing the President, Secretary, and Treasurer. The secretary issues share certificates, opens the corporate minute book, and maintains the stock transfer ledger. If the Certificate of Incorporation does not name the initial directors, the incorporator must execute a written instrument appointing the directors before the organizational actions are effective.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous written consent of the initial directors meeting
Adopted Bylaws of the Corporation
Share certificates and stock transfer ledger
Officer appointment certificates and signed acceptance forms
Director consent letters and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director cannot be reached or objects, reconvene with a quorum as specified in the Bylaws; a unanimous written consent signed by all directors is valid without a meeting. Any drafting defect in the minute book may be cured by a corrective written consent ratified by all directors and filed in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Endorsement and Non-Resident Status Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Tax and Revenue Administration, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an Application for a Taxpayer Identification Number together with a Non-Resident Corporation Status Declaration confirming that the Corporation will derive no income from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands and will conduct all manufacturing, sales, and logistics activities outside RMI territory. Upon acceptance, the Corporation receives the TIN and an acknowledgment of its tax-exempt status under the Income Tax Act 1989. If an RMI atelier is later established, the Corporation must separately obtain the conditional environmental, labor, and business licenses described below; otherwise, the Corporation's overseas manufacturing site must maintain host-country industrial and export permits.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Corporate resolution electing non-resident domestic status
Non-Resident Corporation Status Declaration form
Taxpayer Identification Number application form
Affidavit confirming no RMI-source revenue and no local physical operations
Evidence of host-country manufacturing licenses and export registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax and Revenue Administration queries the non-resident status, furnish a written affidavit with supporting evidence of the absence of local contracts, RMI-source revenue, and physical presence other than the registered office; if the declaration is filed late, no income tax penalty accrues where no tax is due, but a delayed TIN may postpone corporate bank account opening.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Resources and Development (Division of Commerce and Industry) and Ministry of Finance (Business License Office) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands; jurisdiction is engaged only if a physical casting workshop is established within RMI territory, while the non-resident corporation's actual manufacturing site is governed by the host country's industrial licensing authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: RMI Business License Certificate under the Business License Act 1990 and, if applicable, a Manufacturing Operation Permit for small-batch toy and game accessory production; the manufacturing of handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid-core dice at a foreign production site requires the host country's manufacturing license and not an RMI operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA), established under the Environmental Protection Act 1984
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA is mandated for a non-resident domestic corporation performing all manufacturing outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Should a local atelier be established in the RMI, the project will be screened under the RMI Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 1996 and classified as a Class II Registration facility requiring an Environmental Compliance Certificate, given the small-batch epoxy resin casting process and the absence of large-scale hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Uncured epoxy resin, liquid core, and hardener must not be discharged to jurisdictional waters, storm drains, or public sewers; where any aqueous discharge is permitted, wastewater pH must be held between 6.0 and 9.0 and oil and grease below 15 mg/L; fugitive VOC emissions from resin mixing, pouring, and curing must be captured by local exhaust ventilation with a target of no more than 20 ppm at the worker breathing zone; all solid resin waste must be fully cured and disposed through the RMI solid waste system or a licensed recycler, and chemical storage must comply with the RMI Hazardous Chemicals Management Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the RMI Fire and Rescue Services, Ministry of Internal Affairs, verifying fire exits, extinguisher placement, and segregation of epoxy resin and peroxide hardeners; structural load inspection under the adopted RMI Building Code for casting tables and liquid-core storage racks; and occupational clearance under the RMI Occupational Safety and Health Act 2007, including a Chemical Hygiene Plan, ventilation performance testing, maintenance of Safety Data Sheets for epoxy resin and amine hardeners, and an annual workplace safety audit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office (RTO), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; corporate registration and annual-report filings are administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance; official government portal: https://rmigovernment.org
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate a domestic Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990 through a licensed RMI registered agent by filing Articles of Incorporation (no minimum capital requirement); the Registrar of Corporations issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Step 2 — File the annual corporate report and pay the statutory annual fee (currently USD 250 for a non-resident domestic corporation); a Certificate of Good Standing is issued upon compliance. Step 3 — No automatic tax identification is generated at incorporation; an RTO TIN is required only if the corporation derives income from sources within the RMI, employs RMI-resident workers (triggering income-tax withholding and RMI Social Security registration), or lodges customs entries as importer/exporter. Step 4 — A non-resident offshore BC engaged exclusively in foreign e-commerce sales (Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal) does not apply for an RTO TIN; its tax identity is evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation together with the Section 253 non-residence declaration. Step 5 — A Foreign Investment Business License under the Foreign Investment Business Act 1988 is required only for commercial operations physically conducted within RMI territory, which is not contemplated for this offshore tabletop-gaming accessories model.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: Non-resident domestic Business Corporation (Section 253, Business Corporations Act 1990) is exempt from all Marshall Islands income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, and distribution taxes on income derived outside the Republic; RMI taxation is territorial/source-based, so sales of polyhedral dice, game accessories, and IP licensing revenue to overseas consumers fall outside the RMI tax net; the only compulsory state charge is the annual corporate registration fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime exists under RMI law. Available statutory mechanisms: (a) Section 253 election — for status as a non-resident domestic corporation, effected by filing a sworn non-residence declaration with the Registrar of Corporations; (b) Part V continuation (redomestication) election to migrate a foreign corporation into an RMI Business Corporation; (c) election to operate as a resident domestic corporation, which remains taxable on RMI-source income unless the non-resident exemption applies. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the RMI BC is a per se corporation defaulting to C corporation treatment; a Form 8832 check-the-box election is unavailable, and no OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch election is applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No Value Added Tax, Goods and Services Tax, or Sales and Use Tax regime is in force in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Indirect taxation is confined to customs import duties under the RMI Tariff Act and excise duties on alcohol, tobacco, and petroleum fuels, administered by the RMI Customs Service, Ministry of Finance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST exists, and therefore no turnover threshold triggers indirect-tax registration in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. A general business license and foreign-investment business license are required only for commercial operations physically conducted within the RMI; the offshore non-resident BC selling tabletop RPG dice exclusively to foreign customers owes no indirect-tax registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — the RMI has not implemented real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing APIs, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. Customs declarations are lodged on standard paper or electronic formats with the RMI Customs Service; the taxpayer must retain books, records, invoices, and export documentation for a minimum of five years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Structural non-applicability: the RMI levies no VAT/GST, so no zero-rating claim, output-tax charge, or input-VAT refund mechanism exists for exported goods (hand-cast polyhedral dice and tabletop gaming accessories) or offshore services (IP licensing and digital fulfillment). Exports leaving RMI customs territory are automatically export-duty-free; duty-free status is presumptive and requires only ordinary customs supervision plus documentary proof of physical departure from the Republic.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (RMI Customs Service export entry)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List describing the polyhedral dice castings
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from the Marshall Islands
Bank SWIFT credit advice / Inward Remittance Certificate, or payment-platform settlement report (Stripe, PayPal/Braintree payout record) evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin (optional, where preferential tariff treatment is claimed in the destination market)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating refund exists to claw back; the RMI imposes no exchange-control regime and no statutory FX repatriation deadline, the 180-day figure being retained as the documentary standard applied by banking counterparties for export-proceeds substantiation. Enforcement exposures comprise: (i) customs misdeclaration and smuggling penalties (seizure, forfeiture, and fines of up to twice the duty evaded) under RMI customs regulations; (ii) retroactive revocation of the Section 253 tax exemption where the Registrar or RTO determines that the corporation carried on business in, or held real property within, the RMI, thereby exposing previously exempt foreign-source income to RMI income tax assessment plus interest and penalties; and (iii) corporate delinquency sanctions, including administrative strike-off, for failure to file annual reports within the statutory filing window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not maintain a central bank. The official financial-sector regulator is the Banking Commissioner of the RMI Ministry of Finance, exercising powers under the Banking Act 1991 and the Financial Institutions (Licensing and Supervision) Act 2000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender of the Marshall Islands; there are no exchange controls restricting current or capital account transactions. Both capital inflows and outflows are fully convertible and unconditional. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted and are not subject to any withholding tax, exchange permit, or central bank approval. The only practical hurdle is standard bank-level compliance with international correspondent banking due-diligence requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation timelines in the Marshall Islands. A non-resident Business Corporation may retain 100% of its export receipts in any jurisdiction, in any currency, without obligation to remit or convert into local currency. This is consistent with the RMI's full dollarization and absence of an exchange-control regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The RMI has no standalone electronic-money institution or payment-institution licensing framework. Non-bank fintech and offshore digital EMI providers cannot directly access the RMI's national clearing infrastructure. Any cross-border fintech solution must be contractually structured through a licensed RMI commercial bank or a U.S.-chartered bank with a correspondent relationship. Offshore digital EMIs are generally rejected for onboarding into the RMI banking market because of the FATF increased-monitoring listing and the absence of a domestic EMI authorisation path.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly mandated for all beneficial owners and signatories of a non-resident Business Corporation. At least one individual director or a duly authorized officer must appear in person before a bank officer at a BOMI or Bank of Guam branch in Majuro or Ebeye for the initial KYC interview. Remote video opening is not generally available as a first step; it may be considered only after an existing relationship is established and enhanced due-diligence documentation is accepted. Pure online account opening for a non-resident RMI BC is currently unavailable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: RMI is on the FATF increased-monitoring (grey) list, causing correspondent banks to apply enhanced due diligence to all RMI-licensed or RMI-registered entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the RMI Business Corporations Division certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, registered agent's details, audited or internally prepared financial statements, a physical local office address, and a written explanation of commercial purpose describing the manufacturing, molding, and global direct-to-consumer sales of epoxy-resin RPG dice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident tax-exempt status with zero income tax may trigger a shell-company red flag for money-laundering or tax-evasion concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Nonresident Business Corporations Act tax exemption certificate, a credible business plan for tabletop gaming accessories, commercial contracts with raw-material suppliers and distributors, order histories from Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal, plus evidence of operating substance such as inventory purchases, shipping invoices, and logistics records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin dice could be misclassified as adult gaming or gambling-related products, which many payment processors and banks disallow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain product-category documentation demonstrating that the dice are tabletop role-playing game accessories, not gambling equipment. Include material safety data sheets for epoxy resin, finished-product photography, certificate of origin, and a written compliance policy limiting sales to customers age 18 and over.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border digital payment flow through Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal can generate unexpected chargeback thresholds or enhanced review by the acquiring bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a full transaction-flow ledger reconciling all marketplace settlements to the corporate bank account, a chargeback management plan, a clear refund and shipping policy, and historical marketplace performance reports evidencing low chargeback ratios and legitimate fulfilment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan injections must be routed as USD wire transfers over the SWIFT network using an MT103 message to the BC's Marshall Islands bank account. The payment purpose field should reference 'Corporate Capitalization' or 'Equity Contribution' together with the company name and the registered agent's document number. Because the RMI imposes no exchange control, no central bank pre-authorization is required. The receiving bank will perform source-of-funds verification by requesting the sending bank's KYC details, a certificate of incumbency for the BC, and board resolutions approving the injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for imported epoxy resin, silicone molds, pigments, and packaging will use SWIFT MT103 USD wires to suppliers in China, Japan, and the United States. For large or recurring raw-material procurements, a commercial documentary letter of credit (UCP600) may be issued by the RMI bank through its correspondent network. Marketplace sales proceeds from Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal are first settled into the BC's US-dollar pooled settlement account and then cleared by bank wire to the operational account for supplier payments and operating expenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR forward contracts with a licensed international counterparty to hedge European customer receipts
USD/JPY non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts to hedge yen-denominated supplier costs without requiring JPY funding
USD/AUD cross-currency swaps to manage Australian distributor settlement exposure
USD/GBP deliverable forwards to cover United Kingdom PayPal and Kickstarter settlement volatility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation License Renewal / Registration Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (via licensed Registered Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the anniversary of incorporation; failure to pay triggers a late-filing grace period of 60 days after the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty accrues at 10% per month up to a 50% maximum; continued nonpayment results in administrative strike-off or dissolution and loss of Certificate of Good Standing within 3 to 6 months after the anniversary date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Confirmation and Registered Office Address Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent, acting on behalf of the Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each annual renewal, immediately prior to the anniversary date; any change of registered office or registered agent must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government filing fee, but failure to maintain a current registered agent and registered office in the Marshall Islands results in loss of good standing and may lead to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Records Retention Confirmation (Books, Records, and Board Minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the corporation's registered office or principal place of business; available for inspection by the Registrar upon written demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No filing deadline; records must be continuously maintained for at least 7 years from the date of each transaction or corporate action.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to produce statutory records upon lawful demand can expose directors to personal liability and civil penalties, but does not itself cause administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation with authorized capital at or below USD 50,000 and no public-interest, regulated, or financial-licensing activity. An independent qualified audit becomes compulsory if the corporation has gross assets exceeding USD 1,000,000, is a regulated financial entity, or is expressly required by its Articles of Association or a licensed activity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP when audited financial statements are prepared; the Marshall Islands does not issue a separate local GAAP for non-resident domestic business corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The directors must annually deliver to the registered agent a current register of members and a current register of beneficial owners as of the anniversary date. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the register of members and notified to the registered agent within 30 days of the transfer; the annual confirmation must certify the identity and shareholding of all members and beneficial owners after all transfers in the preceding year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 annual professional fee for registered agent, registered office, and UBO register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 typical certified audit fee for a small non-resident single-entity corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 40% of net taxable income for resident corporations; non-resident corporations are taxed only on Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI)-source income at 3% of gross income (or 40% of net income from an RMI trade or business); a non-resident domestic corporation (NRDC) deriving no income from RMI sources and conducting no business in the RMI has zero taxable income and a 0% effective rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective tax for NRDCs under the Income Tax Act 1989 (RMI Revised Code Title 54): foreign-source business income, overseas manufacturing profits, and capital gains from non-RMI assets are entirely exempt; no branch profits tax, no payroll tax on foreign employees, and no undistributed profits tax; the NRDC classification under the Business Corporations Act operates as a statutory offshore exemption, with the annual franchise fee as the only recurring charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1120-RMI) filed with the RMI Tax Administration, Ministry of Finance, via the authorized e-filing portal or paper lodgment; for an NRDC with no RMI-source income, the operative annual filings are the Nil Income Tax Declaration, the Annual Franchise Tax Report, and the Economic Substance (ESR) Annual Declaration filed with the Registrar of Corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The income tax return is due on or before the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the taxable year (April 15 for a calendar-year corporation); the Annual Franchise Tax Report and ESR declaration are due on or before the anniversary of incorporation of the NRDC; tax must be paid in full with the return, and no extension of time to pay is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI real estate, RMI business operations, RMI-source rentals).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report nil or only RMI-source amounts; attach a schedule listing Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal revenues by operating jurisdiction to prove foreign-source character of the dice casting business.
Enter nil where no RMI-source income exists; do not deduct foreign production costs (epoxy resin, molds, labor) on the RMI return, as doing so creates a false filing position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the corporation is a non-resident domestic corporation with no RMI office, employees, bank accounts, or trade or business in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be executed by a director or authorized officer; a false certification is a criminal declaration and triggers full 40% corporate tax exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of 40% corporate rate on net taxable income or 3% gross-basis tax on non-resident RMI-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NRDC with nil income computes zero income tax; if any RMI-source revenue is admitted, remit the applicable 3% gross tax with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of whether any relevant activity under the RMI Economic Substance Regulations is carried on.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Handmade polyhedral dice casting (ISIC 3240 manufacturing) is not a listed relevant activity; select no relevant activity and avoid incidental headquarters or distribution activity conducted from the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory annual franchise tax calculated on authorized share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the Registrar fee for the first tranche of authorized shares with the Annual Franchise Tax Report; late payment triggers administrative dissolution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the tax return attracts a per-month monetary surcharge on the unpaid tax plus interest at 2% per month; non-payment of the annual franchise tax leads to automatic revocation of the certificate of incorporation after administrative notice; willful failure to file or false filing is a criminal offense carrying fines and imprisonment; restoration of a dissolved NRDC requires payment of all arrears plus restoration fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%. The RMI Income Tax Act imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; distributions by an NRDC are characterized as foreign-source and escape RMI tax entirely.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No double taxation agreement (DTA) network exists: the RMI has not concluded any comprehensive income tax treaties, so no treaty-relief application or tax residency certificate protocol is available. Where a shareholder's home jurisdiction demands proof of tax status, the NRDC obtains a Certificate of Good Standing and a Certificate of Incumbency from the RMI Registrar plus a letter confirming non-resident domestic corporation classification; the shareholder then claims unilateral foreign tax credit or exemption in its residence jurisdiction based on the nil-withholding certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate on royalties and interest paid to non-residents, with no treaty rate applicable due to the absence of DTAs; caution: if the royalty or interest is derived from sources within the RMI (for example, licensing an RMI-based business), the 3% gross-basis non-resident tax applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not prescribed. The RMI has no codified transfer pricing documentation regime and no Local File or Master File thresholds in USD. As defensive market practice, an OECD-aligned Local File threshold of USD 10 million consolidated group revenue is adopted where the NRDC intercompany-transacts; a de minimis NRDC with nil RMI-source income files no transfer pricing documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), in force since 1 January 2019, apply to all licensed entities carrying on a relevant activity. Handmade polyhedral dice casting (ISIC 3240 manufacturing) is not a listed relevant activity; however, the NRDC must still file the annual ESR declaration and must not inadvertently conduct a distribution and service centre or headquarters activity from the RMI (for example, an RMI-based director managing global distribution logistics would trigger the ESR test). The actual production, personnel, and decision-making should remain in the jurisdiction of real manufacturing to satisfy foreign economic substance rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a nil or NRDC-exempt return while actually selling dice into, or sourcing income from, the RMI; concealing RMI-source income; executing a false NRDC exemption declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 100% of the underpaid tax plus interest accruing at 2% per month; criminal conviction carries a fine of up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment for up to five years; the corporate charter may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax deficiency and penalties; individuals face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and extradition exposure in the jurisdiction of actual business conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the NRDC as a letterbox entity with no real production, no active bank account, no registered office substance, and no ESR declaration, while using RMI incorporation to evade foreign tax disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR sanctions include monetary penalties of up to USD 30,000 per failure and strike-off or dissolution; the entity may be listed on EU and OECD non-cooperative jurisdiction registers, triggering defensive measures by counterparties and denial of banking, Stripe, PayPal, and Kickstarter services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined for ESR declaration failures; continued operation of a sham entity exposes directors to foreign anti-avoidance assessments and fraud liability in the shareholders' residence jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Fraudulent Use of Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing Kickstarter, Stripe, or PayPal crowdfunding proceeds into a personal bank account without corporate books, structuring transactions to conceal the beneficial owner, or using the NRDC to launder misappropriated funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under RMI anti-money laundering law, legal persons face criminal fines of up to USD 5 million and responsible individuals face imprisonment; civil asset forfeiture and Suspicious Transaction Report investigations by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit apply; Stripe and PayPal impose permanent bans and fund freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The sole director is in practice the beneficial owner; personal criminal liability, travel bans, and restraint orders attach, and directors of NRDCs are exposed to UBO-registry disclosure penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Commmingling of Funds / Piercing the Corporate Veil
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying personal tabletop-gaming expenses, personal travel, or informal member distributions from the corporate account without board resolutions or documentation, leaving the NRDC undercapitalized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Equitable subordination and disregard of limited liability: creditors and tax authorities may pierce the veil under RMI courts applying Delaware-based Business Corporations Act jurisprudence; retroactive corporate tax is assessed on the de facto business and dissolution proceedings may be commenced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for civil restitution of diverted amounts plus punitive damages; in flag-of-convenience jurisdictions the director may face personal bankruptcy declarations and travel-ban orders.
